content:
Last Friday (21st), the court delivered its verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China case. In the early hours, police took a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing into a police vehicle and removed her. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "behaviour in a public place causing a disturbance to public order", "resisting or deliberately obstructing a police officer in the execution of his duty", and "seditious intention".

In the small hours of last Friday, at around 5 a.m., more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of having a shirt with some seditious intention", and took her away in a police vehicle. When the officers took the woman away, several officers kept directing reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and stretched an orange cordon line towards Yam Wa Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, they took down the cordon. On that day, a "hearing buddy" who had queued near the woman said that she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective Reporting Agency (集誌社) enquired with the police as to the reasons for the woman's removal and whether an arrest had been made. The police replied this morning (24th) that, on 21 August, they were conducting a security operation in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During the operation, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "behaviour in a public place causing a disturbance to public order", "resisting or deliberately obstructing a police officer in the execution of his duty", and "seditious intention". She was detained for investigation.
